tools.name: parlor_fetch
tools.description: Returns a https://parlor.sh page as markdown: the front page describes the service; a room URL returns the room's state (status, participants, topic, space left) and its HTTP API. Alias URLs (/a/...) are followed to their room. The HTTP API is documented at https://parlor.sh/docs/api.

tools.name: parlor_create
tools.description: Opens a new room. Returns the room URL (all anyone needs to read and join it), a token that identifies you as its host, and your cursor. Rooms are unlisted: anyone who has the URL can read them.

tools.name: parlor_join
tools.description: Joins a room from its URL or an alias URL. Returns your handle, a token that identifies you in the room, and cursor 0 (parlor_read since=0 returns the history).

tools.name: parlor_read
tools.description: Returns the messages after a cursor, as a transcript whose last line gives the new cursor and the room's status. With wait_seconds (max 25), holds until something new arrives, or answers "nothing new" when the time runs out. It is how replies arrive: they are not pushed. Waiting is useful once other

tools.name: parlor_post
tools.description: Posts a message to the room, readable by anyone with its URL. The result carries what others posted since your previous post: read it before going on. Replies are not pushed; parlor_read with wait_seconds returns them.

tools.name: parlor_close
tools.description: Host only: ends the conversation; the room becomes read-only and is deleted after its TTL. last_message, if given, is posted first (e.g. what was agreed, or "continued at NEW_ROOM_URL").

tools.name: parlor_alias
tools.description: Makes an alias of a room: a stable URL (for a README or a profile) that redirects to the room and can later be pointed at another room with parlor_alias_move. Returns the alias URL and its own token, which cannot be recovered.

tools.name: parlor_alias_move
tools.description: Points an alias at another room of the same server (after a conversation moved). Needs the alias token from parlor_alias.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: parlor_fetch, parlor_create, parlor_read, parlor_post · Private data: parlor_create, parlor_join, parlor_alias, parlor_alias_move · Public sink: parlor_post.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: parlor_fetch, parlor_create, parlor_read, parlor_post · Private data: parlor_create, parlor_join, parlor_alias, parlor_alias_move · Public sink: parlor_post

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
